ProspectResearchClient_s07.t18: We read your homepage to understand what you sell and who buys it. AI with Google Search then looked for companies that match that ideal customer and had a dated public signal in the last 12 months, removed your own company, anything you excluded and duplicates, and kept the strongest ten. Each one was then researched separately against the same seven questions.
ProspectResearchClient_s07.t19: Every answer links to the page it came from. Before you saw them, the links were checked automatically: a link that no longer works was removed and the answer marked down one step, and so was an answer whose page does not name the company. Some sites block automated checks; those links are kept and marked as not checked. “No evidence found” means the search did not find it, not that it does not exist. “Likely” means the evidence is older, indirect or partly confirmed. Contact names are not included; the role shown is who usually owns the problem.
ProspectResearchClient_s07.t21: Fit is out of 100: matching your ideal customer 25, said it will invest in the area you serve 20, hiring for roles you help with 20, funding in the last 12 months 15, a new leader in the buyer's role 10, a new product or market 10. A “yes” earns the full points and a “likely” half. Already using a competitor or doing it in-house is a risk and takes off 15 for a yes, 7 for a likely. Timing is out of 10: funding in the last 90 days 3 (older 2), stated investment 2, hiring now 2, a new leader 2, a new product or market 1.
ProspectResearchClient_s07.t22: AI research can be wrong. Check a source before you act on it. The companies named here have not reviewed or endorsed this research.
